messages:
DeployBot: INCIDENT ALERT — Canary rollout v12 -> model-x: p99 latency breach > 2.5s for last 5m (auto-page)
InfraBot: paging Maya (eng-oncall) :rotating_light: @Maya you are on primary oncall
Maya: on it, grabbing dashboard links
Maya: quick context — canary v12 started rolling 20m ago, traffic shift +10% to canary pool
Sahil: saw initial qps increase but thought autoscaler would handle it
Liam: I've got tracing open, looks like streaming tails are stalling on KV cache hits
Maya: Prometheus query coming — checking p95/p99 across regions
Maya: query: ``sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"runtime\",le!=\"+Inf\"}[5m])) by (le)`` (translated into p95/p99) — raw numbers:
```
region-us-east p95=450ms p99=2.7s
region-us-west p95=420ms p99=2.6s
region-eu p95=380ms p99=1.8s
```
Maya: streaming stall alarms are showing high tail for streaming endpoints (streaming_push and stream_token) — looks correlated to model-x encoder KV fetch latency
Anya: logs show a lot of `KVCache miss, fallback to disk` and `KV shard busy` in the same timeframe
Liam: here's a top-level span example (copied):
```
span: encode_tokens -> wait_for_kv_cache_shard (latency 800ms) -> tpu-kernel-run 50ms
```
Maya: hypothesis: new tokenizer/encoder layout in v12 increased KV key cardinality -> causing lock contention on shard hosts
Sahil: are we sure it's KV locks and not batch packing changes? rollout didn't change batching config AFAIK
Liam: checked commit diff for v12: encoder tokenizer mapping changed; also small change to kv key prefix `enc_v2:` -> increases hot keys
Maya: impact: p99 > SLO for canary traffic, some user streaming connections are seeing stalls/keepalive dropouts. Not yet full customer-facing outage but risk of SLO breach for whole service if we continue.
DeployBot: Rollout metadata — started: 1739875443, canary fraction: 10% -> warming to 25% scheduled in 10m
Maya: mitigation proposals:
- Option A: Pause rollout and rollback canary to v11 (fast, known-good)
- Option B: Throttle canary traffic back to 5% and propagate patch to decoder that reduces KV key cardinality
- Option C: Emergency scale-up of KV cache nodes (takes ~15-20m)
Nina-CS: internal note — one enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) reported slow streaming responses 2x their threshold, prepping customer comms if this escalates
Anya: we can try a quick KV shard drain/rehash to reduce hotspots but that is risky mid-rollout
Sahil: can we test a config flip to disable prefix caching for model-x instances? that would avoid the hot key pattern temporarily
Liam: yes, we have a runtime flag `--kv-prefix-cache=false` per model runtime. Can flip at canary pool level via rollout manager.
Maya: priority order I'd do: pause rollout -> set runtime flag on canary pool -> monitor 5m -> rollback v12 if no improvement or continue if fixed
DeployBot: Action by policy: pause-rollout request sent (automated) — waiting manual confirmation
Maya: confirming pause-rollout now (using /rollout pause canary v12)
DeployBot: Rollout paused (by Maya) — canary traffic frozen at current fraction
Maya: patching canary pool runtime flags: applying `--kv-prefix-cache=false` to pool-canary-eu and pool-canary-us-east
Liam: applying via infra command:
```
for node in $(list-canary-nodes); do ssh $node "sudo systemctl set-env RUNTIME_FLAGS=--kv-prefix-cache=false && sudo systemctl restart runtime"; done
```
Anya: rolling restart started, shall we drain connections first? restart will gracefully reconnect streaming clients
Maya: doing staggered restarts, 30s pause between nodes
Maya: initial metrics after first few nodes restarted (1m after): p99 us-east dropped from 2.7s -> 1.1s
Sahil: p95 stable, p99 improving — good sign
Liam: traces show KV wait time dropped from ~800ms -> ~120ms after env flip
Nina-CS: sending heads-up to AcmeCorp about mitigation in progress, will update in 15m
Nina-CS: message sent: "We observed elevated tail latency for streaming in a limited canary rollout. We've paused the rollout and applied a mitigation. Monitoring now; will follow up with final status." (internal CS ticket #CS-8931)
Maya: will monitor for 10m, if stable we can either proceed with a patch and resume rollout or rollback. prefer patch since v12 has other improvements
Anya: creating ticket for encoder team to reduce key cardinality and add telemetry (#ENG-encoder-402)
DeployBot: automated audit log: pause-rollout (Maya), env-flip (Maya), node-restarts (Liam)
Maya: update 10m after mitigation: p99 us-east 980ms, us-west 950ms, eu 440ms — overall within SLO for canary traffic
Sahil: recommendation: hold rollout paused. encoder team to deliver patch to reduce hot prefixes; after patch, run a small canary re-deploy to 3% then ramp
Nina-CS: will draft customer follow-up: summary + ETA for fix (ETA 3-8h depending on encoder team)
Maya: handoff to daytime oncall Sahil in 8m for continuous monitoring. @Sahil you own watch for next 2h, escalate back if tail reappears
Sahil: ack, taking watch. I'll keep the paused rollout and the runtime flag until encoder fix deployed or until infra says scaling is needed
Liam: leaving traces and a small runbook for rollback steps in the incident doc
Maya: final note: PagerDuty incident closed (severity reduced) — we'll mark this as partial SLO breach avoided thanks to quick mitigation. Follow-ups:
- ENG-encoder-402 (reduce KV key cardinality)
- ENG-infra-993 (add auto-eviction for hot key patterns)
- CS-CS-8931 (customer notification thread)
Nina-CS: confirmed customer will be updated when patch is merged
DeployBot: thread closed (automated) — if you need to reopen, react with :rotating_light:
